item.title: Version 2.6.0
item.description:
IndieGent 2.6.0

Lazy Tasks is now IndieGent. New name, new mark, new look and a first-class dark mode — plus an Inbox that brings work to you, project summaries that write themselves, and a Garden that finally explains what a day was.

Nothing moved on your Mac. Your projects, sessions, schedules, Tank's memory, your licence and every permission you've granted all carry over — the bundle identifier and the settings folder deliberately keep their old names, so this is a rename you read rather than something you redo.

  • A new name, mark and look — the Dock, menu bar, About and Quit items, window title, onboarding, Settings and your agents' session briefs all say IndieGent. The app wears its own icon and its own type (Plus Jakarta Sans and Inter, both shipped inside the app): white where the page is, warm beige on the surfaces, one accent yellow spent only on the thing you're meant to click.
  • Dark mode — the app finally follows your Mac's appearance instead of pinning itself to light.
  • The name reaches everything the app sends out — PRs your sessions open are signed by IndieGent, operator runs introduce themselves as IndieGent, the licence email says IndieGent, and the download arrives as IndieGent-2.6.0.dmg.
  • The Inbox — a new section at the top of the sidebar shows work coming in: an issue assigned to you, an @mention, a review someone's waiting on, with an unread count on the bell. Click through to GitHub, or start a session on an issue right from the row.
  • Sidebar counts are yours, not everyone's — the badge counts issues assigned to you plus unclaimed ones; a teammate's work sits beside it as a plain number. Home and Tank follow the same rule.
  • Every project can say what it is — write a project's one-line summary yourself, or let IndieGent read the repo's README and draft it for you. Home gathers the blank ones under "projects with no summary", and "Draft them all" does the lot.
  • The Garden explains itself — run the cursor along the chart and each day tells you what happened: sessions, issues picked up, PRs shipped, agent time and which repos. Quiet days answer too. The card now lines up with Field Notes at every window size.
  • Suggested clears itself — a confirmed suggestion ticks, shows the issue number it was filed as, then slides out of the queue. An empty queue is now a designed screen: when the next run fires, when suggestions last arrived, and a Run now button.
  • Open issues read oldest first — sorted by issue number, lowest at the top, the same way every time.

item.title: Version 2.5.0
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.5.0

LazyTasks now plans ahead, not just executes. Put Tank on a schedule, review what it proposes from a new Suggested queue, and let the built-in nightly review turn today's closed issues into tomorrow's tasks — nothing touches your repos until you say yes.

  • Scheduled operator tasks — a new SCHEDULED sidebar section holds standing orders ("Mon–Fri 9pm: review closed issues and suggest tasks") that run headlessly in the background. Full editor with prompt, time picker, day-of-week chips, optional project focus, and one-time runs; each entry shows its next run in plain words and how the last run went. Missed runs get one catch-up ask on launch — never a silent skip, never a double-run.
  • Suggested queue — scheduled runs deposit draft GitHub issues (up to 3 per run) into a new Suggested sidebar section instead of acting on your repos. Review the title, project, and "why", edit if you like, then Confirm to file the issue in one click — or Dismiss to bury the idea permanently; dismissed ideas are never suggested again.
  • Nightly review built in — Mon–Fri at 9pm, Tank reviews every issue closed since its last successful run and proposes up to 3 follow-up tasks, each with a "why now" tied to the issue or PR that prompted it. Nothing meaningful closed? It proposes nothing.

item.title: Version 2.4.3
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.4.3

The sidebar stays put. Fixed the sidebar getting cut off when selecting a project after resizing the window.

  • Sidebar no longer clips — selecting a project could shave the left edge off the sidebar when its deploy row demanded more width than the window had. The row now wraps on narrow windows, and the main content area can never push the sidebar off-screen again.

item.title: Version 2.4.2
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.4.2

The window behaves after a resize. Enlarging the window no longer leaves dead space, and shrinking it back no longer squishes the sidebar.

  • Home fills the window — enlarging the window makes the home view expand to the full width instead of holding a fixed-width column with dead space on the right.
  • Sidebar rows stay put — project rows and group headers truncate long names to one line, so selecting a project can no longer make its row render wider than the sidebar (the cause of the post-resize sidebar squish).
  • Model selection documented — the README now explains setting a project's default model and overriding it per dispatch.

item.title: Version 2.4.1
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.4.1

Headless sessions are back on their feet. 2.4.0 could pick up a stale claude install and fail every headless dispatch — this release fixes that, surfaces real error messages in session notes, and freshens the model picker's suggestions.

  • No more stale claude in headless runs — tool resolution now probes your interactive shell first, so the CLI your terminal uses (nvm/fnm/asdf installs included) wins over an older copy elsewhere on the PATH. Headless dispatches that died with "exit 1" on 2.4.0 work again.
  • Failure notes show the real error — when a tool prints its error to stdout (as claude -p does), the session note now includes that text instead of a bare exit code.
  • Current model aliases — the model picker menus now suggest fable, opusplan, opus[1m], sonnet[1m] and friends alongside opus/sonnet/haiku. Still free text, so any model name the CLI accepts works.

item.title: Version 2.4.0
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.4.0

You pick the model, you pull the trigger. Choose which model a session runs with — per project or per dispatch — and get a confirming click before anything ships. Plus headless sessions now start on every Mac, however node is installed.

  • Choose your model — set a project default from the model chip on the project page (pick a suggestion or type any model name the CLI accepts), override any single dispatch from an issue row's "Start session with model" menu, and Tank can pass "model" on a start_session action. Nothing set means the provider default, as before.
  • Ship asks first — the first click on any Ship control arms it (amber, "Ship?"); a second click within 3 seconds ships, anything else disarms it. No more accidental ships.
  • Headless works on nvm-only Macs — background sessions no longer die with "env: node: No such file or directory" when node lives in nvm/fnm/asdf: the runner now resolves tools through your interactive shell, so it sees the same PATH your terminal does.

item.title: Version 2.3.0
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.3.0

Background sessions become dependable. Headless runs now start from any issue row, survive every Mac's environment, can't silently lose work — and the new Running board keeps every session on one screen.

  • Running board — a new sidebar entry (⌘3) shows every agent session across all your projects, grouped by project with the ones that need you on top. Ship, reopen, discard, or dismiss straight from there.
  • Background sessions from issue rows — a moon button next to Start session runs the issue headless: no terminal window, and the finished PR still closes the issue on merge (Pro).
  • Headless runs hardened — background agents now get your terminal's PATH instead of dying on launch, a wrap-up that can't count commits keeps the workspace instead of deleting it, failed runs release their issue claim, and agents answer to a leash: stoppable, auto-stopped at 45 minutes, and never left orphaned after quit.
  • Headless housekeeping — Tank's state marks sessions headless vs terminal and separates the ones wedged with unpushed work, status files no longer leak, same-second dispatches can't collide on a branch name, and free-tier background requests fall back to a terminal session and say so.
  • Multi-session dispatch fixed — sessions of one project now take turns for the shared git cache, so a 5-session dispatch starts 5 sessions instead of failing half with lock errors.
  • Shipped issues leave the lists — three races that let closed issues linger in OPEN ISSUES and My issues are fixed: refreshes queue instead of dropping, stale fetches can't overwrite fresh ones, and shipped issues are tombstoned.
  • Welcome back — returning users get a brief branded splash instead of the toolchain checklist; it only reappears when something actually broke, redesigned with copyable fix commands.
  • Shortcuts you can see — key-cap badges on buttons, a ⌘/ cheat sheet under Help, and a jump to System Settings to rebind anything.
  • Settings in the sidebar foot — a proper labelled row (⌘,) where Macs keep it, instead of a tiny gear in the PROJECTS header.
  • Secrets sheet fixed — focus lands in the KEY field, Return walks and submits, incomplete adds say what's missing, and saves confirm.

item.title: Version 2.2.0
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.2.0

The first fully stable multi-session release. Running several agent sessions at once is now safe end to end — and 2.2.0 leans into it.

  • Multi session — a new button above the open issues list turns the rows into checkboxes: select the issues you want worked in parallel and start one agent session per issue, each linked to its issue so wrap-up PRs close the right one. A toggle switches bulk runs to the background (Pro).
  • Shipping in a row no longer strands PRs — ship now catches the session branch up with main first, so back-to-back sessions all merge; when a merge genuinely can't happen, the session lands as "Needs merge" with the reason instead of a false "Done".
  • Agent profiles — give sessions a working persona (Senior Engineer, Test Engineer, Docs Writer, and more), edit them in the new profile studio, set a project default from the Profile chip, or pin one to a single issue. Profiles are plain markdown files you can share between Macs.
  • Keyboard shortcuts everywhere — ⌘↩ submits the composer and deploy panel, a real menu bar makes everything discoverable and rebindable: New Issue (⌘N), New Session (⇧⌘N), Go to Home (⌘1), My Issues (⌘2), projects (⌘3–⌘9), Refresh Issues (⌘R), and more.
  • Quieter project header — Secrets, Cloudflare, and Fresh/Cached controls now sit as small capsule chips on the repo · branch line, fading to faint outlines when at their defaults.
  • The Garden grows with you — new users see a compact daily bar chart of sessions instead of a barren 24-week grid; the familiar weekly heatmap takes over as history accumulates.

item.title: Version 2.1.4
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.1.4

  • Concurrent sessions fully isolated — each session on a cached project now runs in its own git worktree (private files, index, and branch), so simultaneous sessions can no longer trample each other's work. Wrap-up also refuses to commit unless the workspace is on the session's own branch.
  • Live session status on issue rows — while a session for an issue is in flight, its row shows a status chip ("Session running", "Needs input", "Wrapping up") instead of the Start session link, in both Open Issues and My Issues.
  • Agent Time on the home screen — a fourth stat card totals the wall-clock time agents have spent working across your wrapped-up sessions.
  • Collapsible New Session panel — click the panel header to collapse it down and keep your open issues front and center. The choice sticks across projects and restarts.
  • My Issues stays up to date — the list and its sidebar badge refresh the moment anything changes your queue, re-check in the background every couple of minutes, and refresh when you switch back to the app.

item.title: Version 2.1.3
item.description:
LazyTasks 2.1.3

  • Per-project secrets — projects can hold secret variables (API keys, admin credentials) so agents in fresh workspaces can run the app they're working on. Add keys via the SECRETS badge or import a .env from the clipboard. Values are write-only and never leave this machine; key names sync so a second Mac shows what still needs entering.
  • Per-project Cloudflare accounts — assign an account once per project and every session runs wrangler as that account. Profiles share the ~/.cf-profiles convention; tokens never leave the machine.
  • Issue editing + self-assign — edit issues right from LazyTasks, and new issues assign to you by default. Description fields are now proper multi-line editors.
  • A livelier home — issues handled, PRs shipped, day streak, "The Garden" contribution heatmap of your sessions, and Field Notes with fun facts from your ledger.
  • Shipping tidies up — "Ship it" closes the session's terminal window, and self-merged issues vanish from Open Issues immediately.
  • Instant issue actions — create, edit, label, assign, and close apply on the spot, reconciled against GitHub behind the scenes.
